The `circuitBreaker` parameter passed into the lambda is never used. The `example` state is created with a separate 100 MB breaker, and `createUsingParamsFrom(example)` registers the new state against `example.breaker` (the 100 MB one). Consequently, when the helper adds data to the returned state, it only touches the 100 MB breaker, so the small-limit breaker created by `testCircuitBreakerTrip` is never exercised. The test will always succeed on the first iteration without ever triggering a `CircuitBreakingException`, making it a no-op that provides no real coverage of the trip-and-release path.
Consider either:
- Creating `example` with the `circuitBreaker` parameter supplied by the helper, or
- Writing a dedicated test that directly asserts on the breaker actually used by `createUsingParamsFrom`.

If you use the cranky breaker service it'll blow up *randomly* and you can assert that you always freed the memory, no matter the random explosion. I rather like it for this sort of thing.


Which one of your tests hits a the breaker exception you are guarding?

> Which one of your tests hits a the breaker exception you are guarding?

The `testReadWithData()`. The reserve is only called when it has data in it. So I added that one explicitly.

About the cranky breaker, I'm not sure we want it to break randomly. This has multiple potential breaking points I wanted to test (Add memory and release on error, on every constructor).

The cranky breaks 1/20 times. If we're fine with this one (The full suite takes around 1 second on my machine), I would leave it as-is. It tests every potential breaking point (_Divided in 16 random seeds_).
Is it too much? Not sure

>About the cranky breaker, I'm not sure we want it to break randomly. This has multiple potential breaking points I wanted to test (Add memory and release on error, on every constructor).

That's where the cranky is really good at.

Just updated it to use the cranky breaker. It will fail ~1/5 times, so I guess it's ok. I suppose even 1/20 times would be ok for something like this.
I guess I was reinventing the wheel here XD
